column1: Good. So where were we last time?
column2: 好的。那么上次我们讲到哪里了？

column1: Last time we determined what all the algebraic integers were in the field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d})$, where $d$ was a square-free integer;   and the algebraic integers formed a ring we'll call $R$, and in the case—there were two possible cases.
column2: 上次我们确定了代数整数环的所有元素——在数域 $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d})$ 中（其中 $d$ 为无平方因子整数）； 这些代数整数构成一个环，我们记为 $R$。这里有两种可能的情形。

column1: Well, there was the case where you always contained all integers plus integer multiples of $\sqrt{d}$, and that was all you got when $d$ was congruent to 2 or 3 mod 4.
column2: 其中一种情形总是包含所有整数，加上 $\sqrt{d}$ 的整数倍，而当 $d \equiv 2$ 或 $3 \pmod 4$ 时，你得到的就只有这些。

column1: And in the case where the—the $d$ was congruent to 1 mod 4, you got a little more: so you certainly got the integers, you got the multiples of $\sqrt{d}$,
column2: 而在 $d \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ 的情形下，你得到的东西要多一点：你当然得到了整数，得到了 $\sqrt{d}$ 的倍数，

column1: but you also got the multiples of $(1 + \sqrt{d})/2$ when $d$ was congruent to 1 mod 4.
column2: 但你也得到了 $(1 + \sqrt{d})/2$ 的倍数，当 $d \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ 时。

column1: So in particular the algebraic integers form a ring,   and that ring is the ring we're going to study from now on.
column2: 特别地，代数整数构成一个环， 这个环就是我们从现在起要深入研究的环。

column1: Now there's a uniform way of writing this, a nice uniform way of writing it.
column2: 现在有一种统一的书写方式，一种非常优美的统一步骤。

column1: So in other words, the things in the algebraic integers are of the form $a + b\sqrt{d}$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers,   or $a$ and $b$ are half-integers which are not integers—they both have to be either integers or half-integers.
column2: 换句话说，代数整数环中的元素具有形式$a + b\sqrt{d}$，其中 $a$ 和 $b$ 都是整数， 或者 $a$ 和 $b$ 都是非整数的半整数——它们必须同为整数或同为半整数。

column1: And this occurs when $d$ is congruent to 1 mod 4, because the multiples of this number have $a$ and $b$ both half-integers, neither integers, right?
column2: 这发生在 $d \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ 时，因为这个数的倍数其 $a$ 和 $b$都是半整数，而不是整数，对吧？

column1: If you—well, if you multiply by 2, then $a$ and $b$ are integers, but if you multiply by 3, $a$ and $b$ are half-integers.
column2: 如果你——好吧，如果你乘以 2，那么 $a$ 和 $b$ 是整数；但如果乘以 3，$a$ 和 $b$ 就是半整数。

column1: So these are the set of algebraic integers.
column2: 所以这就是代数整数集合。

column1: Now the uniform way of writing this is to introduce a new number,   which is a better number for describing this ring of integers: capital $D$, which is either $4d$ or $d$.
column2: 现在统一书写它的方法是引入一个新数， 一个能更好描述这个整数环的数：大写 $D$（判别式），它要么是 $4d$，要么是 $d$。

column1: This is the case when $d$ is congruent to 1 mod 4, and this is the case when $d$ is congruent to 2 or 3 mod 4,
column2: 当 $d \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ 时取 $d$，而当 $d$ 同余于2 或 $3 \pmod 4$ 时取 $4d$；

column1: in which case this number here becomes congruent to 0 mod 4.   So this capital $D$ is either divisible by 4 or has remainder 1 mod 4.
column2: 在那后一种情形下，这里的这个数变为同余于 $0 \pmod 4$。 因此这个大写 $D$ 要么被 4 整除，要么模 4 余 1。

column1: And then if you introduce that, there's a uniform way of writing down this ring of algebraic integers.
column2: 引入它之后，就有了书写该代数整数环的统一方法。

column1: You can write it like this—this is a cute way of doing it: it's all multiples of 1 and all multiples of $(D + \sqrt{D})/2$.
column2: 你可以把它写成这样——这是一种很巧妙的表示方法：它由 1 的所有倍数以及 $(D + \sqrt{D})/2$ 的所有倍数构成。

column1: Now why is that? Because first of all, the square root of $D$ is either equal to $2\sqrt{d}$ or $\sqrt{d}$, depending on what happens.
column2: 为什么会这样呢？因为首先，$\sqrt{D}$ 要么等于 $2\sqrt{d}$，要么等于 $\sqrt{d}$，取决于具体情形。

column1: So in the case where $d$ is congruent to 1 mod 4, this is $(d + \sqrt{d})/2$, but little $d$ is odd, so you can subtract an integer from it and get this number,   and conversely if you had this number, you could add an integer to it and get that number.
column2: 那么在 $d \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ 的情形下，这正是 $(d + \sqrt{d})/2$；但小写 $d$ 是奇数，所以你可以从中减去一个整数得到这个数， 反之，如果你已知那个数，也可以加上一个整数得到这个数。

column1: So this ring is the same as this ring when capital $D$ is odd.
column2: 所以当大写 $D$ 为奇数时，这个环与原环完全相同。

column1: If capital $D$ is divisible by 4, so $\sqrt{D} = 2\sqrt{d}$, then both this number and this number are divisible by 2.
column2: 若大写 $D$ 能被 4 整除，则 $\sqrt{D} = 2\sqrt{d}$，此时分子中的两项都能被 2 整除。

column1: You can divide the 2 out, and you're left with an integer plus a multiple of $\sqrt{d}$, so you can express $\sqrt{d}$ and vice versa.
column2: 约去 2 后，你就剩下一个整数加上$\sqrt{d}$ 的倍数，因此可以互相表示。

column1: So this is the uniform way of describing the ring of algebraic integers, and we could call this $R_D$ or something like that.   That's why I say it's easier to index by this capital $D$ than it is by the little $d$.
column2: 因此这就是描述代数整数环的统一方法，我们可以把这个环记为 $R_D$ 之类。 这就是为什么我说用大写 $D$ 来作为指标比用小写 $d$ 更方便。

column1: So for example, now we're going to study these in particular when $D$ is negative:   they're called imaginary quadratic rings.
column2: 例如，现在我们要特别研究 $D < 0$ 的情形： 它们被称为虚二次环。

column1: And we're going to see right away at the beginning of this lecture   why this is an easier case than the negative—than the positive.
column2: 在本讲一开始我们就会立刻看到， 为什么这比负——比正判别式的情形要容易得多。

column1: And if you list out the possibilities for $D$ that are less than 0, as I did last time,   they look like $-3, -4, -7, -8,$ $-11$ ($-12$ is no good),
column2: 如果像我上次那样列出所有小于 0 的 $D$ 的可能取值， 它们依次是 $-3, -4, -7, -8,$$-11$（$-12$ 不行）、

column1: $-15$ ($-16$ is), $-19, -20, -23$, etc.   So there are an awful lot of interesting rings indexed by this.
column2: $-15$（$-16$ 不行）、$-19, -20, -23$ 等等。 因此这里有非常多的由这些指标标记的有趣环。

column1: And this case here, this $D = -4$, is where $d = -1$, and that's the Gaussian integers.
column2: 这里的这一项 $D = -4$ 对应于 $d = -1$，那就是高斯整数环。

column1: So that's the case we've looked at,   and all these other cases are new rings that are going to be interesting for us to study.
column2: 这是我们已经研究过的情形； 而所有其他情形都是全新的环，它们对我们来说非常值得探讨。

column1: So does everyone see how just taking an integer, defining a ring like this,   you get an interesting ring which may or may not have unique factorization, which we're going to want to study?
column2: 大家都看明白了吗：仅凭选取一个整数并定义这样一个环， 你就得到了一个有趣的环，它可能具有也可能不具有唯一因子分解，这正是我们要研究的。

column1: Okay. Now the first thing to show you   why this case is easier than the positive case, which are called real quadratic rings: let's just observe that we have the following map.
column2: 好的。现在首先要向大家展示的是， 为什么这种情形比正数情形（称为实二次环）要容易得多：让我们观察一下存在如下映射。

column1: I claim we have a map $\Delta$, which Artin calls the norm map—that's the usual notation for it— from the ring $R$ to the ring $\mathbb{Z}$ in any of these cases.
column2: 我断言存在一个映射 $\Delta$，Artin 称之为范数映射（也是其常用记号），在所有这些情形下它都从环 $R$ 映到整数环 $\mathbb{Z}$。

column1: And the map looks like this: it takes something of the form $a + b\sqrt{d}$ and if I want to take the norm of it, I take it to $a^2 - d b^2$.
column2: 映射形式如下：它将形如$a + b\sqrt{d}$ 的元素映为它的范数：$a^2 - db^2$。

column1: In other words, that's the product of this number $a + b\sqrt{d}$ with the other number $a - b\sqrt{d}$.   If this thing is called $\alpha$, then this number in the ring is called $\alpha'$.
column2: 换句话说，这正是这个数 $a + b\sqrt{d}$ 与另一个数 $a - b\sqrt{d}$ 的乘积。 如果前一个元素记作 $\alpha$，那么后一个环中元素记作 $\alpha'$。

column1: There's a way of taking the ring to itself which takes this number to, in some sense, its conjugate.
column2: 存在一个从该环到自身的自同构，将这个数映为某种意义上的共轭。

column1: And if you multiply these two numbers in the ring, notice that the terms before $\sqrt{d}$ go away,   because you have $-ab\sqrt{d}$,
column2: 如果你在环中将这两个数相乘，会注意到 $\sqrt{d}$ 前面的交叉项抵消了， 因为你有一项带负号的 $-ab\sqrt{d}$，

column1: but here you have $ab\sqrt{d}$ with a plus sign, so you just get a normal number.   Now I claim that number is an integer.
column2: 而这里有一项带正号的 $+ab\sqrt{d}$，所以你只得到一个普通的数。 现在我断言该数是一个整数。

column1: That's not completely obvious:   it's completely obvious in this case when $a$ and $b$ are both integers, but you have to check that it's an integer when $a$ and $b$ are both half-integers.
column2: 这并不是显然成立的： 当 $a$ 和 $b$ 都是整数时显然成立，但当 $a$ 和 $b$都是半整数时你必须验证它也是整数。

column1: But if $a$ and $b$ are both half-integers, then the fact that $d$ is 1 mod 4 means that this number turns out to be an integer.
column2: 不过若 $a, b$ 都是半整数，由 $d \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ 的事实，意味着这个数最终确实是一个整数。

column1: I mean, a priori it's 1/4 of an integer, but you—you'll check, you see that $a^2$ is congruent to 1 mod 4, and $b^2$ is congruent...   So you'll see that this number turns out to be an integer.
column2: 我的意思是，先验地看它是某个整数的四分之一，但你检查一下就会发现：$a^2 \equiv 1 \pmod 4$，且 $b^2$ 同余…… 所以你会发现这个数最终确实是一个整数。

column1: So in particular, this product of the number $a + b\sqrt{d}$ times this other number is an actual integer.
column2: 特别地，数 $a + b\sqrt{d}$ 与另一个数相乘的积是一个真正的整数。

column1: And this map, which takes elements of our quadratic ring to elements in the normal ring,   has the nice property that if you take the norm of a product, it's the product of the norms.
column2: 并且这个将二次环的元素映到普通整数环的映射， 具有优良的性质：乘积的范数等于范数的乘积。

column1: We saw this in the Gaussian numbers.   And the reason is that this norm of a product is just $\alpha \alpha'$ times $\beta \beta'$.
column2: 我们在高斯数中见过这一点。 原因是乘积的范数就是 $\alpha\alpha'$乘 $\beta\beta'$。

column1: Well, really, sorry, it's $(\alpha\beta)(\alpha\beta)'$,   and you find that $(\alpha\beta)'$ is $\alpha' \beta'$, and then you rearrange it, and then you rewrite it
column2: 好吧，严格说是 $(\alpha\beta)(\alpha\beta)'$， 你会发现 $(\alpha\beta)' = \alpha'\beta'$，然后重排各项，

column1: as $(\alpha\alpha')(\beta\beta')$,   using the fact that multiplication is commutative in this ring, and then you recognize this is the norm of $\alpha$ and this is the norm of $\beta$.
column2: 将其改写为 $(\alpha\alpha')(\beta\beta')$， 这里利用了该环中乘法的交换性，于是你认出这正是 $\alpha$ 的范数乘上 $\beta$ 的范数。

column1: So it's multiplicative: it's not additive, but at least it's multiplicative.   Okay, so this will allow us to identify, as we did in the Gaussian numbers, what the units of the ring are.
column2: 所以它是可乘的：它不是可加的，但至少是可乘的。 好的，这能让我们像在高斯数中那样确定环中的单位元是什么。

column1: Ah, one more observation,   and this is the reason that for $D < 0$, this is the reason that this condition becomes so nice: if you look at the norms, this is an integer,   but when we're in the imaginary quadratic case,
column2: 啊，还有一个观察， 这正是为什么对于 $D < 0$，条件会如此好——这正是其性质极佳的原因：查看范数，它是一个整数， 但当我们处于虚二次情形时，

column1: it's a non-negative integer, because this is a square, this is a square, and we have a $-d$ here,   so we're taking the sum of positive numbers.
column2: 它是一个非负整数，因为这一项是平方，这一项也是平方，而且这里有 $-d$（$d < 0$）， 所以我们取的是两个正数的和。

column1: So this really makes the imaginary quadratic case so much easier: the norm is non-negative.   Now I claim we have the following result on units, and this is true in all cases.
column2: 这就是让虚二次情形容易得多的本质原因：范数是非负的。 现在我断言，关于单位元有如下结论，且这在所有情形下都成立。

column1: Proposition: $\alpha$ is a unit in $R$—sorry, in the ring $R$—if and only if the norm of $\alpha$, which is $\pm 1$, is a unit in $\mathbb{Z}$.
column2: 命题：$\alpha$ 是环 $R$ 中的单位元，当且仅当 $\alpha$ 的范数（即 $\pm 1$）是 $\mathbb{Z}$ 中的单位。

column1: Okay, so that you can test whether this thing is invertible in the ring by calculating this integer and seeing whether it's invertible in the integers.
column2: 好的，因此你可以通过计算该整数并观察它在整数环中是否可逆，来检验该元素在环中是否可逆。

column1: Proof: If $\alpha$ is a unit, there exists a $\beta$ in the ring where $\alpha \beta = 1$.
column2: 证明：若 $\alpha$ 是单位，则环中存在 $\beta$ 满足 $\alpha\beta = 1$。

column1: That's what a unit means. Apply the norm:   then the norm of $\alpha\beta$, which is the norm of $\alpha$ times the norm of $\beta$, is the norm of 1.
column2: 这就是单位的定义。两边取范数： 则 $\alpha\beta$ 的范数即 $\alpha$ 的范数乘 $\beta$ 的范数，等于 1 的范数。

column1: But the norm of 1 is just 1,   because $b = 0$ and $a = 1$.
column2: 但 1 的范数就是 1， 因为 $b = 0$ 且 $a = 1$。

column1: So here are two integers whose product is 1.   Therefore the norm of $\alpha$ has to be a unit in the integers, and consequently the only units in the integers are $\pm 1$.
column2: 于是这是两个乘积为 1 的整数。 因此 $\alpha$ 的范数必须是整数环中的单位，从而整数环中仅有的单位是 $\pm 1$。

column1: Conversely, if the norm of $\alpha$ (which remember is $\alpha \alpha'$) is equal to $\pm 1$, then $\pm \alpha'$ is an inverse for $\alpha$.
column2: 反之，若 $\alpha$ 的范数（即 $\alpha\alpha'$）等于 $\pm 1$，则 $\pm\alpha'$ 就是 $\alpha$ 的逆元。

column1: And this element is in the ring too, because if $a + b\sqrt{d}$ is in the ring, then $a$ and $b$ are both integers or half-integers;   consequently these are both integers or half-integers, so this is in the ring.
column2: 并且该元素也在环中，因为如果 $a + b\sqrt{d}$在环中，那么 $a$ 和 $b$ 同为整数或同为半整数； 从而共轭项也同为整数或半整数，所以在环中。

column1: And that gives you the inverse, because here's a thing that you multiply it by:   you either get $+1$, in which case $\alpha'$ is an inverse, or you get $-1$, in which case $-\alpha'$ is an inverse.
column2: 这就给出了逆元，因为拿它相乘： 要么得到 $+1$，此时 $\alpha'$ 是逆元；要么得到 $-1$，此时 $-\alpha'$ 是逆元。

column1: Okay. Thus, corollary: if $D < 0$, then $\alpha$ is a unit   if and only if the norm of $\alpha$ is $+1$, because in that case we saw the norms are all non-negative, so it can't be $-1$.
column2: 好的。因此推论：若 $D < 0$，则 $\alpha$ 是单位元 当且仅当 $\alpha$ 的范数为 $+1$，因为在那类情形中我们看到范数全是非负的，所以不可能是 $-1$。

column1: All right, now let's enumerate the units in the negative case. In fact, if $D = -3$, there are 6 units;   if $D = -4$, there are 4 units; and if $D < -4$, there are 2 units.
column2: 好的，现在我们来列举负判别式情形下的所有单位元。事实上，若 $D = -3$，有 6 个单位元； 若 $D = -4$，有 4 个单位元；而当 $D < -4$ 时，只有 2 个单位元。

column1: In fact, in this case the unit group is the same as the unit group of $\mathbb{Z}$,   just $\pm 1$.
column2: 实际上在这些情形下，单位群与整数环的单位群相同， 仅仅是 $\pm 1$。

column1: So for almost all these cases, except for the first two, you don't get any new units in the ring that you didn't know about:   nothing is invertible except when $a$ is equal to $\pm 1$ and $b = 0$.
column2: 所以对于几乎所有这些情形（除前两种外），你在环中都得不到任何未知的全新单位元： 除了当 $a = \pm 1$且 $b = 0$ 之外，没有其他元素可逆。

column1: All right, let's prove it. Well, we're looking for solutions.
column2: 好的，我们来证明它。我们在寻找方程的解。

column1: Proof: A unit $\alpha = a + b\sqrt{d}$ is a solution to $a^2 - d b^2 = 1$, where $a$ and $b$ are either integers, or they're half-integers.
column2: 证明：单位元 $\alpha = a + b\sqrt{d}$ 是方程 $a^2 - d b^2 = 1$ 的解，其中 $a$ 和 $b$ 要么都是整数，要么都是半整数。

column1: Okay, now look at this: if $b = 0$, right,   then $a^2$ has to be 1, so $a = \pm 1$, and there you get the units in $\mathbb{Z}^\times$,   those things we already knew about.
column2: 好，现在看这里：如果 $b = 0$，对吧， 那么 $a^2$ 必须等于 1，所以 $a = \pm 1$，这就得到了 $\mathbb{Z}^\times$ 中的单位元， 即我们早已熟知的那些元素。

column1: If $b \ne 0$, I'm sorry,   then $-b^2 d$ is greater than or equal to $-D/4$, right?
column2: 如果 $b \ne 0$（不好意思）， 那么 $-b^2 d$大于或等于 $-D/4$，对吧？

column1: Because whatever $b$ is, $|b| \ge 1/2$, so $b^2 \ge 1/4$, so it's $-D/4$, how about that?   Because $b$ has got to be a half-integer, so this has got to be $-D/4$.
column2: 因为无论 $b$ 取何值，$b$ 的绝对值都至少为 $1/2$，所以 $b^2 \ge 1/4$，因此该项至少是 $-D/4$。 因为 $b$ 必须是半整数，所以这至少是 $-D/4$。

column1: Once $-D$ is bigger than—if, if if $-D > 4$, it's hopeless, right?
column2: 一旦 $-D$ 大于——如果，如果如果$-D > 4$，就绝无可能了，对吧？

column1: Because then this number will be bigger than 1,   and there's no way that these things can add up to 1—this number is positive, right?
column2: 因为那样该数就会大于 1， 这两项绝不可能相加等于 1——各项都是正的，对吧？

column1: So that eliminates almost everything, and then you just check these two cases and you find the various solutions—a finite number.
column2: 所以这排除了几乎所有情况，然后只需检查这两种情形，便能得到有限个解。

column1: On the other hand, look at what happens if $D$ is positive: if $D$ is positive,   this is the difference of a square and some multiple of a square, right?
column2: 另一方面，看看当$D$ 为正时会发生什么：若 $D > 0$， 这就是一个平方与平方倍数的差，对吧？

column1: So you could certainly imagine that difference being 1 no matter how big $a$ and $b$ are.   I mean, they're not adding up: you're taking a square minus $d$ times a square.
column2: 所以你完全可以设想无论 $a$ 和 $b$ 有多大，差值都可能为 1。 我是说，它们不是相加：而是一个平方减去 $d$ 乘平方。

column1: And in fact, it turns out that if $D$ is positive, there are always an infinite number of units.
column2: 事实上可以证明，若 $D > 0$，总存在无限多个单位元。

column1: In fact—which I'm not going to prove—if $D > 0$, $R^\times$ is infinite, and that gives a lot of headache.
column2: 事实上——虽然我不打算在此证明——若$D > 0$，则 $R^\times$ 是无限群，这会带来很多麻烦。

column1: I'll give you an example, this first simple example: Example: $d = 5$. That's the smallest positive $d$.   So there $R = \mathbb{Z} + \mathbb{Z} \frac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}$.

column2: 周五，Peter 将向大家展示如何在这些环中挽救唯一因子分解，因为那是19 世纪中叶数学家们的一项重大发现： 当时发现元素无法总是分解为素元（我们刚才看到了例子），但你可以把理想分解为素理想的乘积！

column1: Namely, there was a generalization of multiplication for ideals; then there was a generalization of irreducible elements that took place for ideals, called prime ideals;   and that every ideal could be written uniquely as a product of prime ideals. That's a huge result!
column2: 也就是说，理想之间定义了乘法运算；随后有了素元向理想的推广——称为“素理想”； 并且每个理想都能唯一分解为素理想的乘积。这是一个极其重大的成果！

column1: And then Peter will also show you how you measure how far one of these rings is away from being a unique factorization domain;   and that's something I've worked on a lot, and I'll talk to you about that on Monday. Okay, see you then!
column2: 接着Peter 还会告诉大家如何度量这类环距离唯一分解整环有多远（理想类群与类数）； 这正是我深入研究过很多的内容，我会在下周一跟大家讲。好的，周一见！
